goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:130 — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` bypasses the whole sanitization pipeline; `cooked` is attacker-controlled HTML rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (best.html.erb:19). `absolutize_urls` rewrites, does not sanitize → stored XSS / account takeover. (conf 90)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a new `cook_method` that can be set to `:raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). When `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). `TopicEmbed.import` and `import_remote` create posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`, using content sourced from RSS (`SimpleRSS.parse ... i.content`) or scraped HTML (`Readability::Document#content`). The only processing done is `absolutize_urls`, which rewrites relative href/src but does not remove scripts/unsafe tags. In the embed view (app/views/embed/best.html.erb) the post body is rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any unsafe HTML stored in `raw`/`cooked` for these imported posts can execute in the client context (stored XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:34-38 — `revise!` return value discarded, then `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` fires unconditionally; a failed/skipped revision permanently marks the embed "in sync" and it can never resync. (conf 100; also data-migration)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking whether `revise!` actually made any change. From the diff, `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` early (`return false if not should_revise?`), so a skipped/failed revision would still update `content_sha1`. That would make future polls think the embed is up-to-date and stop attempting to resync, even though the underlying post content wasn’t updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` return ignored; `revise!` now returns true when the save silently failed — sentinel meaning changed for all existing callers. (conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `PostRevisor#update_post` changes `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. However, `@post.save`’s return value was already ignored before this change, and `revise!` did not previously use the save result as a sentinel return value (it has no explicit success return; it still only early-returns `false` when `should_revise?` is false). The change only toggles validation behavior when `:skip_validations` is set; it does not newly cause `revise!` to return `true` on a failed save in a way that differs from prior behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs a *global* hourly feed poll inline from a *per-URL* request-triggered job; throttle key is per-URL, so N missing embeds → N full feed re-imports. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `TopicRetriever` is invoked per missing `embed_url` (via `EmbedController` enqueuing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), and the only throttle in `TopicRetriever` is a Redis key scoped to `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), not global to feed polling. Therefore, requests for many different missing embed URLs can each trigger a full `poll_feed` run, which parses the entire feed and iterates all items (`rss.items.each`) and calls `TopicEmbed.import` for each item, causing repeated full-feed work N times. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:48 / poll_feed.rb:29 — external HTTP with no timeout, no size cap (`.read` into memory), no rescue, no circuit breaker; a hung remote pins a Sidekiq worker. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. The diff introduces multiple remote fetches via `open-uri` without any explicit timeouts, size limits, or error handling:
- `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (topic_embed.rb ~48), which reads the entire response body into memory and will block the job/thread while waiting for the remote server/connection.
- `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (poll_feed.rb ~29), similarly blocking on a remote request and consuming the full feed content.
Neither call is wrapped in rescue/retry logic; any network hang/slow response or exception can tie up a Sidekiq worker (at least for the duration of underlying library defaults) and potentially cause large memory usage due to unbounded reads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-30 — check-then-`create!` TOCTOU against the unique index with no `rescue RecordNotUnique`; concurrent retrievals commit a duplicate Topic/Post, then the job dies leaving an orphan topic with no embed row → recreated on every subsequent request. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: TopicEmbed.import does have a race (it does `where(embed_url: url).first` then later `TopicEmbed.create!` with a unique index on `embed_url`), so concurrent imports of the same URL can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` because there is no rescue. However, the finding’s claimed outcome (“commit a duplicate Topic/Post, leaving an orphan topic with no embed row” and “recreated on every subsequent request”) is not verifiable from the diff: the creation path is wrapped in `Topic.transaction do ... creator.create ... TopicEmbed.create! ... end`, so if `create!` fails due to the unique index, the transaction should roll back the post/topic creation as well, preventing an orphan. Also once one embed row exists, subsequent requests will find it via `topic_id_for_embed` and won’t recreate it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:78-79 — `embed_url` uniqueness is raw exact-string; no canonicalization (http/https, trailing slash, utm params, fragment) → same article yields multiple topics, splitting discussion. This is the core gap given the task title. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: `topic_embeds.embed_url` is enforced unique via a DB unique index, and all lookups use exact-string matching (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url)` / `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`), but the code never normalizes/canonicalizes URLs (scheme, trailing slash, query params like `utm_*`, fragments, etc.). Since `TopicEmbed.import`, `import_remote`, `PollFeed`, and `TopicRetriever` all pass through the URL as-is, the same underlying article reachable via multiple equivalent URLs will create multiple `TopicEmbed` rows/topics, splitting discussion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` added to an already-shipped migration; emits `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics` on any redo/reset, and prod never receives the change. Unrelated to embeds. (conf 100; also scope, intent, feasibility)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics` in an existing migration. That will cause Rails to emit a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics` before creating the table *when that migration's `up` runs*. However, the finding’s core claim that this is a real defect because it was “already-shipped” and “prod never receives the change” is not verifiable from the diff (we can’t know release/shipping status). Also, `db:migrate:redo` already drops the table via the migration’s `down` (drop_table), and `db:reset` drops/recreates the DB anyway, so the added `force: true` doesn’t clearly introduce a new correctness/security bug based solely on this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` is irreversible in effect: rollback drops the only record of which posts hold raw HTML, mangling every imported post on next cook. Also a full-table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `posts` (the sibling migration in this same diff uses the safe batched pattern). (conf 100 / 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration that does `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL (which Discourse uses), adding a non-null column with a default historically triggers a full table rewrite and an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the table, which is a real operational risk for a large `posts` table; this contrasts with the batched/lock-aware approach seen in other migrations in the diff. The claim about “irreversible in effect” is weaker (Rails can rollback by dropping the column, and losing that data is the normal consequence of dropping a column), but the locking/table-rewrite concern is a concrete, verifiable issue introduced by this migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3,11 — `force: true` on the sole store of the embed_url↔topic mapping; `add_index ... unique: true` can fail on duplicates after create succeeds, and the natural re-run then wipes the mapping → duplicate topics for every already-imported article. (conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates a brand-new `topic_embeds` table and only then adds a unique index on `embed_url`. In the normal (and intended) first-run execution, there is no preexisting data in the table, so the `add_index ..., unique: true` cannot fail due to duplicates “after create succeeds” because no duplicates can exist in an empty, just-created table. The finding’s scenario (index creation failing from duplicates, then re-run dropping already-imported mappings via `force: true`) would require the table to have already been populated with duplicate `embed_url` rows before the index is added, which is not supported by the diff’s migration flow. While `force: true` is generally destructive if a migration is re-run, the specific failure mode described is not a verifiable problem introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_topic_embeds.rb:4-5 — `topic_id`/`post_id` have no FK, no cascade, no `dependent: :destroy`; a deleted topic leaves a row that 500s `TopicView.new` for every visitor and permanently blocks re-import of that URL via the unique index. (conf 75; also architecture, completeness)

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` integer columns and only a unique index on `embed_url`; there are no foreign keys or ON DELETE cascades, and the `TopicEmbed` model’s `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` has no `dependent:` cleanup shown. In `EmbedController#best`, the code trusts `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and immediately calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` when a row exists; if the referenced topic/post is deleted and the `topic_embeds` row remains, this can raise (e.g., record not found) and also prevents re-import because `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` bails out on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and the unique index prevents creating a replacement row. The diff does not include any compensating deletion logic for `topic_embeds`, so the finding points to a real defect risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116-148 — unrelated importer rewritten: `--category` CLI flag deleted, `created_at: Date.parse(...)` dropped (archive chronology destroyed), and local import converted to an unguarded live HTTP fetch per thread with no rescue/resume. (conf 100; also intent, architecture, feasibility)

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes the `--category` option and the logic that looked up `category_id`, and replaces the per-thread `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` call with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` (live HTTP fetch) without any rescue/handling in the shown code path, and it does not accept/pass through `created_at` or category, so imported topics/posts will no longer preserve the Disqus thread timestamp nor allow selecting a category via CLI. This is a concrete behavior regression and adds a new failure mode (network/remote fetch exceptions aborting the import).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32-42 — `topic_retriever.expects(:perform_retrieve)` + `expects(:retrieved_recently?)` stub away the unit under test; zero coverage of the redis throttle, `no_throttle`, the `exists?` recheck, or the inline PollFeed branch. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The cited lines in `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` do mock/stub internal methods (`retrieved_recently?`) and assert whether `perform_retrieve` is invoked, so this particular spec does not execute the real Redis throttling logic, the `no_throttle` path, or the `perform_retrieve` internals (including the `exists?` recheck / PollFeed branch). However, that is a test-coverage/design critique rather than a verifiable defect in the production code introduced by this diff; the spec is intentionally written as an interaction/unit test and is not inherently “wrong” or failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:39-42 — update test never asserts `content_sha1` changed; delete `update_column` and it still passes while production re-revises the post every poll forever. No no-change-path test. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the only mechanism preventing repeated revisions on unchanged content is updating `embed.content_sha1` via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` in the update path. The spec at `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` "Supports updating the post" only asserts the returned post has new cooked content, and never asserts that the associated `TopicEmbed` record’s `content_sha1` was updated. There is also no test for the no-change path (same contents should not trigger another revise). Therefore, removing `update_column` would not break the current spec, and the test suite would not catch the regression that causes perpetual re-revisions on subsequent polls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `skip_validations` branch has no test that an invalid revision actually persists, nor that validations still run when absent. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, adding a new conditional validation path. However, the proposed finding is about missing tests for this new behavior, not a concrete bug/security/correctness defect in the code itself. The diff does not show failing behavior, incorrect logic, or broken validations—only that test coverage for the new branch isn’t added here. Lack of tests is a quality concern, but not a verifiable problem introduced by the diff under the given criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-46 — mocks `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`, but the controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`; passes only via inline Sidekiq, and nothing asserts the real behavior (enqueue, `user_id:`, `render 'loading'`). (conf 75; also completeness, intent)

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is grounded in the diff: `EmbedController#best` does **not** call `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`; when `topic_id` is nil it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` and `render 'loading'`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the “tells the topic retriever to work...” example) sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, which the controller itself never invokes. This makes the spec incorrect/fragile (it would only pass if `Jobs.enqueue` executes the job inline during the controller action), and it also fails to assert the controller’s real behavior (enqueuing `:retrieve_topic` with `user_id`/`embed_url` and rendering `loading`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: docs/tasks/task-001.md vs diff — no "embed URL handling/validation system" exists at base; this is a greenfield subsystem (controller, routes, 2 views, JS, SCSS, 2 jobs, 2 gems, 4 site settings, model, migration) plus 3 unrelated files. The only lines touching validation *remove* it. (conf 100; also intent F2/F3)

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is largely a meta observation about scope (“greenfield subsystem”, “plus unrelated files”) and references a file not present in the diff (docs/tasks/task-001.md), which is not a verifiable defect introduced by this change. It also misstates validation changes: the diff adds multiple validation/guard checks for embed URLs/hosts (e.g., EmbedController#ensure_embeddable checks SiteSetting.embeddable_host and referer host; TopicRetriever#invalid_host? validates URI/host), so it’s not true that the only validation-related change is removing validation. The PostRevisor change conditionally skips model validations only when an explicit :skip_validations option is passed, which is an intentional behavior change and not inherently a bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — url interpolated unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>`; and the guard at line 11 uses `^` (line anchor) not `\A`, so `"javascript:alert(1)\nhttp://x"` passes. (conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the URL validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. In Ruby, `^` matches the start of a line, not strictly the start of the string, so a value like `"javascript:alert(1)\nhttp://x"` will match at the `http://x` after the newline and pass the guard. The same untrusted `url` is then interpolated directly into raw HTML: `"#{url}"` without escaping. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` and later rendered via `raw post.cooked`, this can result in HTML/attribute injection (e.g., quotes/newlines in `url` breaking out of the `href` attribute or yielding a `javascript:` URL), making this a real security issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:24-31 — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` on a page rendering the *authenticated* viewer's content, gated only on the spoofable `Referer` header; no CSP `frame-ancestors`, no scheme/port check. (conf 50)
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core security issue: setting `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` disables clickjacking protection and relying on the `Referer` header for gating is bypassable/spoofable. It doesn’t explicitly mention the nil-referer-to-empty-string fallback masking failures, but it captures the main underlying vulnerability described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9-16 — unauthenticated attacker-triggered fetch + public topic creation; throttle keyed on full URL, so `?x=1,2,3…` defeats it entirely. No per-IP limit. (conf 75; also architecture)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new public route `GET /embed/best` (EmbedController#best) does not require authentication and, when no existing TopicEmbed is found, enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` with the attacker-supplied `embed_url` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:12-16). `RetrieveTopic` calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which throttles using a Redis key built from the *full* `@embed_url` string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}` in lib/topic_retriever.rb), so changing query params (e.g., `?x=1,2,3...`) creates distinct keys and bypasses the 60-second throttle. Because `TopicEmbed` uniqueness is on exact `embed_url`, varying the query also bypasses the duplicate check (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`), allowing repeated remote fetches (`open(url).read` in TopicEmbed.import_remote) and creation of new topics/posts. There is also no per-IP limiting in this path; the only gating is a Referer host check in ensure_embeddable, which can be spoofed by non-browser clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — `feed_polling_url` has no scheme/host validation, turning an admin text field into an RCE/file-read sink via `Kernel#open`. (conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with only a `.present?` check. There is no validation that `feed_polling_url` is an http(s) URL (or otherwise constrained), so Ruby's `Kernel#open` semantics allow opening local file paths (e.g. "/etc/passwd") and, more critically, piped commands (strings starting with `|`) via `IO.popen`, which can lead to command execution/file read if an attacker can influence this admin setting. This is a verifiable security defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31-37 — no per-item rescue and no LIMIT on `rss.items`; one bad item aborts the entire poll (with `retry: false`, lost until next hour). (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `rss.items.each do |i| ... content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) ... end` with no per-item `rescue`. Any exception raised while processing a single item (e.g., `i.content` being nil causing `nil.scrub`, malformed fields, or errors inside `TopicEmbed.import`) will abort the entire job and stop processing remaining items. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so Sidekiq will not retry on failure; processing is effectively delayed until the next scheduled run. Also, there is no limit/slicing on `rss.items`, so a very large feed will be processed in one run without bounds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255) under a unique index; long URLs raise `PG::StringDataRightTruncation` and kill the poll. Should be `:text`. (conf 75; also data-migration)

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the column `embed_url` is declared as `t.string`, which in Rails maps to a VARCHAR(255) by default, and a unique index is added on it (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). The code stores full external URLs directly into this field (e.g., `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` in TopicEmbed.import and `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`), with only a regex check for http(s) and no length validation/truncation. If an RSS/Atom entry link (or fetched URL) exceeds 255 characters, PostgreSQL will raise `PG::StringDataRightTruncation` on insert/update, which would cause the polling/retrieval job to fail. This is a concrete schema/code mismatch introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 — `feed_key` has zero call sites: a conditional-GET cache maintained by nothing. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In the added `Jobs::PollFeed` class, `feed_key` is defined but not used anywhere *within this diff*. However, concluding it has “zero call sites” across the codebase can’t be verified from the diff alone (it could be called from existing code not shown). Also, its mere non-use is at most dead/unused code, not a clear correctness/security defect introduced by the change. The “conditional-GET cache” intent is speculative; the method currently just builds a Redis key string and does not implement conditional GET behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 — non-atomic `SETNX` + `EXPIRE`; a crash between them leaves a TTL-less key that throttles that URL forever. Use `SET NX EX`. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then TTL is applied in a separate call `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will persist without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and return `true` (throttled) indefinitely for that embed_url. Using a single atomic Redis command (e.g., `SET key value NX EX 60`) avoids this defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:64 + migration:3 — bare-int discriminator: DB hardcodes `default: 1`, Ruby `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` derives `1` positionally. Reordering silently repoints every row to "emit raw HTML". No validation, no CHECK; post_creator.rb:216 gates on `.present?` so an arbitrary int is written unvalidated. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an integer-backed enum (`Post.cook_methods ||= Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`) plus a DB default (`cook_method` default: 1). However, the finding’s core claim (“reordering silently repoints every row to raw_html”) is hypothetical and not a verifiable defect in this diff: nothing in the change shows a reorder or that `Enum`’s mapping is unstable/position-based in a way that makes `default: 1` incorrect today. The “arbitrary int is written unvalidated” point is technically true (PostCreator assigns `@opts[:cook_method]` directly), but this is internal plumbing and does not, by itself, demonstrate a concrete bug/security issue introduced by the diff. Without evidence that `Enum` maps differently (e.g., 0-based) or that user input can set `cook_method`, the claimed problem is speculative rather than a real, demonstrable issue in the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64-72 — `href.start_with?('/')` corrupts protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.x/a.jpg` → `http://feedhost/cdn.x/a.jpg`); bare relative refs left broken. Untested. (conf 85)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both `` hrefs and `` srcs are rewritten when the attribute `start_with?('/')`. This will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a.jpg`; the code then strips all leading slashes (`sub(/^\/+/, '')`) and prefixes with the feed host (`prefix`), producing `http(s)://feedhost/cdn.example.com/a.jpg`, which is incorrect. Additionally, truly relative references like `images/a.jpg` do not start with `/` and are left unchanged despite the method comment claiming it converts relative URLs to absolute. The added specs only cover root-relative paths (`/hello`, `/images/...`) and do not test these edge cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << "..."` mutates the caller's string and raises on nil (empty feed entry / Readability extracting nothing) or a frozen literal. (conf 85)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents` is assumed to be a mutable `String` and is unconditionally appended to via `contents << "\n<hr>..."`. If `contents` is `nil` (e.g., empty/missing feed entry content or a readability extraction that returns nil), this will raise `NoMethodError`. Additionally, using `<<` mutates the caller-provided string object, which is observable by the caller and can also raise if a frozen string is passed. The diff shows no guard (`contents ||= ""`, `to_s`, or `dup`) before mutation, so the issue is verifiably present in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7-11 — 30s reload with no give-up condition, no attempt counter, no error state; a permanently-failing retrieval reloads and re-enqueues forever. No error locale key exists. (conf 80)

adjudication.rationale: The new `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally does `setTimeout(... document.location.reload() ..., 30000);` with no maximum retries or failure UI. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, it always `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., remote fetch keeps failing or host rejected), the page will reload every 30s and keep hitting `#best`, which in turn keeps enqueueing `retrieve_topic` jobs indefinitely. While `TopicRetriever` has a throttle to avoid repeated *work*, it does not prevent the controller from enqueueing jobs on every reload, and there is no error state/locale/message beyond `embed.loading`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5-17 — no guard for a missing `#discourse-comments` or undefined `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl`; required globals undocumented. (conf 85)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the code immediately does `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)`. If the element is missing, `comments` is `null` and this will throw at runtime. Likewise, it directly references `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` when building `iframe.src`; if either global is not defined, it will raise a `ReferenceError`. There are no runtime guards or fallbacks for these cases in the diff (the `/* global ... */` comments only affect linting, not execution).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile:209-210 — only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` regenerated; the RAILS3 branch (which this tree targets, rails 3.2.12) has no updated lockfile → frozen/deployment installs fail on the two new gems. (conf 60)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two new gems added to `Gemfile` and an updated `Gemfile_rails4.lock` that includes them. However, the finding asserts a problem in a separate “RAILS3 branch” / rails 3.2.12 lockfile not being updated, but no rails3 lockfile (e.g., `Gemfile.lock` or similar) is shown in the diff. From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that this tree targets rails3, that another lockfile exists/should be updated, or that deployment installs would fail due to a missing lock update. What is verifiable is only that the rails4 lockfile was regenerated alongside the Gemfile change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4 — `embed.css`/`embed.js` are new top-level bundles not added to `config.assets.precompile` → `AssetFilteredError`/404 in production. (conf 55)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce new top-level assets (`app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`) and the new layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`. However, the finding’s claim that they are “not added to `config.assets.precompile`” (and therefore will 404 in production) cannot be verified from this diff because no asset precompile configuration is shown/changed here; the project may already precompile all JS/CSS bundles or otherwise include `embed` via existing settings. Thus the alleged production failure is speculative based on code not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open` used without requiring `open-uri` in this file (only poll_feed.rb requires it); via the thor task `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filename → `Errno::ENOENT`. (conf 70)

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb around line 48) but the file does not `require 'open-uri'`. Without open-uri, `Kernel#open` won’t handle HTTP(S) URLs and will instead treat the string like a local filename, typically raising `Errno::ENOENT`. The only added `require 'open-uri'` in this diff is in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, which does not cover callers like the Thor task (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor`) or `TopicRetriever` (`lib/topic_retriever.rb`) that also invoke `import_remote`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18-28 — three "requires" tests all short-circuit on `feed_polling_enabled?` (defaults false, never stubbed true); delete the other two guard clauses and all three still pass. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` runs only if `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the “requires feed_polling_url” and “requires embed_by_username” examples never stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to `true`, so if it’s `false` by default (and `config/site_settings.yml` sets `feed_polling_enabled: false`), execution short-circuits before checking the other two conditions. That makes those two tests ineffective: removing the `feed_polling_url.present?` and `embed_by_username.present?` guards would not cause them to fail under the default setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb — `poll_feed` itself stubbed out in every test: user lookup, parse, URL fallback, `unescapeHTML`, and `import` have zero coverage. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The added spec file `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` gating and that it delegates (or not) to `poll_feed` via `poller.expects(:poll_feed)` expectations; it never calls `poll_feed` to exercise its internal behavior (user lookup, `SimpleRSS.parse`, URL fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML`, `TopicEmbed.import`). So the statement about “zero coverage” for `poll_feed`’s logic is factually accurate. However, this is a test-coverage critique rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect in the production code introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb — new job, no spec: blank-url raise, user lookup, and the `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` mapping all untested. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` and there is no corresponding spec file for it in the added specs (only `topic_retriever_spec`, `embed_controller_spec`, `poll_feed_spec`, `topic_embed_spec`). However, the proposed finding is solely that the job logic is “untested”. Lack of test coverage is not a verifiable functional defect/bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the diff; it’s a process/quality suggestion rather than a concrete code problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js — new executable behavior, zero tests. (conf 100)

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:48-52 — `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil and views aren't rendered, so `response.should be_success` is vacuous; the test would pass with a broken template. (conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example “creates a topic view when a topic_id is found” sets `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` but does not specify a return value. With Mocha, an unmet `returns(...)` means the stubbed call returns `nil`, so the controller assigns `@topic_view = nil`. The corresponding template (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`) dereferences `@topic_view.posts` and `@topic_view.topic`, which would raise if the view were actually rendered. In RSpec controller specs, views are not rendered by default (unless `render_views` is enabled), so the `after` assertion `response.should be_success` can still pass and won’t detect a broken template. This makes the test assertion effectively non-verifying for the template behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a reversed substring check; `e.origin === ""` passes (`indexOf("")` → 0), and there's no `e.source` check. Impact bounded to iframe height. (conf 75)
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core flaw: origin validation is done via a substring search (`indexOf`) rather than strict, parsed origin matching, making it bypassable. The candidate describes it as a reversed/unsafe substring check and gives bypass vectors (e.g., empty origin), which aligns with the golden concern that malicious origins can pass due to `indexOf`-based validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — `request.referer` HTML-escaped into a JS string literal (wrong escaper for script context) and passed as `targetOrigin` despite being a full URL from an untrusted header. (conf 50)
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `request.referer` (a full URL) is being used as `postMessage` `targetOrigin`, which aligns with the golden issue that `targetOrigin` must be just the origin (scheme+host+port) and a full URL will prevent delivery. It adds extra concerns (untrusted header, wrong escaping) but still identifies the same core bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26-29 — `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` branch untested; removing it turns a 403 into a 500 with no test failure. (conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the referer is parsed via `URI(request.referer || '')`. If `request.referer` is a malformed URI, `URI(...)` will raise `URI::InvalidURIError`, which is explicitly rescued and converted into `Discourse::InvalidAccess` (likely resulting in a 4xx). The added controller specs cover missing referer and mismatched host, but do not cover a malformed referer string that triggers the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` path. Therefore, removing the rescue would plausibly change behavior from a controlled 4xx to an unhandled exception (500) without any test failing, because no test exercises that branch.
